newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura's Sakamaki quizzed by prosecutors -- media.
newsitem.headline: Nomura's Sakamaki quizzed by prosecutors -- media.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors have questioned Hideo Sakamaki, former president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, on suspicion that he may have been directly involved in the brokerage's payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, Japanese media reported on Thursday.
A Nomura spokesman had no comment on the reports of the questioning, carried by various news agencies and television stations.

Sakamaki, who resigned as president in March over the scandal and is now an adviser to the giant brokerage, is suspected of ordering former Nomura managing directors to provide 49 million yen of company money to a client linked to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, the Mainichi Shimbun newspaper said in its morning edition on Thursday.
The paper said the Tokyo Prosecutor's office had decided to arrest Sakamaki. A Nomura spokeswoman earlier declined comment on the Mainichi report.

Sakamaki told a parliamentary panel on Wednesday that he briefly met Ryuichi Koike -- the "sokaiya" corporate racketeer at the heart of the scandal -- in 1992. But he denied knowledge of any stock deals by the racketeer through Nomura.
Sakamaki said in April he believed only the two former Nomura executives, now under arrest, were involved in the payoffs.
